scope: Closes the live and supervisor-level gaps left at the FOR-48 integration: a merged PR whose body says Closes #N closes the issue on GitHub and Crewroom records that state separately from workflow state; evidence, PR-link and research-outcome comments delivered live exactly once across a restart; optional workflow labels applied live when configured and not applied when off; the research-completion gate exercised through the supervisor transition.

simulated.provider: Loopback GitHub REST fixture (node:http in scripts/rust/workflow-providers.test.ts); not github.com.
checks: scripts/rust/workflow-providers.test.ts 'native research completion holds a GitHub-sourced run until its outcome comment is queued, then posts it exactly once after stop': the full native Workflow (workflow-fixture example, real crewroom-host processes under tmux with the scripted runner) imports a GitHub issue as a pinned research ticket. After research/submit and research/complete with the team idle and an extra supervisor notify, the run stays running with researchCompletion set and nothing is posted. Once the coordinator (reporter fallback) queues research_outcome through github/report, the supervisor stops every host and completes research; nothing is posted before completion; the ticket's source status stays open; two flushes post exactly one comment labelled verified evidence and the update is confirmed.

Mutation check: replacing the GitHub needs_research_summary condition in supervisor/workflow/transitions.rs with false makes this test fail (the run completes before an outcome is queued); the source was restored before commit.

The Jira counterpart test in the same file still passes, as do 'agent tool authorization enforces ...' and 'pinned research verifies source citations ...' in scripts/rust/workflow-transitions.test.ts.

live.repository: Private disposable sandbox <owner>/crewroom-e2e-sandbox, approved by the operator for this work. Issues #7 and #8 and PR #9 are synthetic. Issue #6 was an aborted first attempt: the probe posted one evidence comment, then its restart step failed to reacquire the local controller lock (fixed in the probe before the recorded run); #6 was closed as not planned and is not part of this evidence.
live.credential: The operator's gh login token passed as CREWROOM_GITHUB_TOKEN, read per request and never printed; each stage asserts its receipt does not contain it.
live.agents: No agent process ran in the live probe. The coding run's attempts carry recorded (never probed) identities; the candidate is a real commit on the sandbox's default branch in a Crewroom run worktree (crewroom-process helper), but its required-check and passing-review receipts are recorded directly, without a container runtime, and readiness is then assessed by Evidence::assess. The research artifact was submitted through Research::submit with a citation verified against the pinned sandbox commit.
live.merge: PR #9 was created by the probe through GitHubPullClient with 'Closes #8' in its body; GitHub reported closingIssuesReferences [8]. The PR was merged on github.com with gh (merge commit) between the publish and merged stages; GitHub then closed #8 itself: the issue's ClosedEvent closer is PullRequest #9, stateReason COMPLETED, closedAt 2026-10-18T10:59:13Z, one second after mergedAt 10:59:12Z. Neither Crewroom nor the probe closed the issue.

lines: The pull request description closes this issue when the PR merges into the default branch.

limitations: The live verified comments come from a ready candidate whose check and review receipts were recorded directly, not from an agent-driven run with a container check; no agent process called github_report live (the probe calls the same prepare path the host tool routes to).
The live PR was created by the probe through the FOR-46 client and merged with gh, not by Crewroom's publication flow end to end.

The restart is a store reopen with rebuilt services in a new process, with confirmed writes rewound to uncertain (evidence, research outcome) or sending (PR link); it is not a SIGKILL of crewroomd mid-request.
The supervisor-level gate test uses the loopback GitHub fixture, not github.com; the live research stage drives the gate predicate and completion directly, not the supervisor loop.
